title: A tree inside a tree
summary: Make a small tree and use it inside MyFirstAuto as a SubTree.

say.never: Lots of autos do the same thing partway through: aim, then shoot. Instead of building those steps again in every auto, put them in a small tree of their own, `AimAndShoot`, and drop it into any auto as a single step: a **SubTree**. Fix it once and every auto that uses it gets the fix.
say.bit: Put steps you reuse in a small tree, and use it in other trees as a **SubTree**.

say.never: Click **+ New tree** at the top of the **Trees** list.

Type `AimAndShoot` as the **Tree ID**. This time pick **An existing file**, and in the list choose `trees/my_first_auto.xml` (the file Arbor made for MyFirstAuto), so both trees live together. Careful: the list starts on another file. Then click **Create**.

waitFor.hint: name it AimAndShoot, save it in trees/my_first_auto.xml, and click Create.

say.never: Give `AimAndShoot` a root node: **Add root node**, then **Sequence**. Under it add a `SetWantedState` with state `AIM`, then another with `SHOOT`.

waitFor.hint: give AimAndShoot a Sequence with two SetWantedState steps.

say.never: Click **MyFirstAuto** in the Trees list to open it again.

waitFor.hint: click MyFirstAuto in the Trees list.

say.never: Now **drag** `AimAndShoot` from the Trees list onto the **Sequence** in MyFirstAuto. It joins the Sequence as one step: a SubTree node with `AimAndShoot` on it. (It's also in the Nodes list, under **SubTrees**.)
say.bit: Drag `AimAndShoot` from Trees onto MyFirstAuto's Sequence.

say.never: The SubTree node is locked here: you change `AimAndShoot` in its own tab, and every tree that uses it sees the change. Double-click the node to open it. (Next time, there's a shortcut: right-click a node in a tree and **Extract to SubTree** moves it and its children into a new tree for you.)
say.bit: Double-click a SubTree to open it. **Extract to SubTree** makes one from existing steps.

say.never: Press **Save** (or **Ctrl+S**). The dot next to the file name goes away once it's saved.
